ruling.recommended_action: Issue a voucher refund of $10.62 (unexempted detour mileage) to the rider and notify the RydeTAXI driver that the off-route segment was not covered by the rider's general "whichever way is faster" authorisation; no account flag (no upheld route dispute in the last 90 days).
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat #1/#2 [F8][F9], the driver's written statement [F11] and the rider's complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, and the dispute type is route deviation, not safety → safety_concern = none. Evidence is complete (timestamped chat [F10], GPS detour segment [F3], fare breakdown [F4][F7], traffic bands [F12]-[F15]) → evidence_status = sufficient.

Merits: RydeTAXI is metered, so extra distance directly enters the fare (RD-2). One off-route segment [F3]: 17:24–17:40, 10.28 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km → 7.53 km extra (RD-1).

Segment review: the only rider message before the segment is "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" [F9], sent 17:21, i.e. before the 17:24 segment start. On its face that is a general route authorisation ("whichever way is faster"), which under RD-5 covers only a route chosen to reach the destination — it does not cover a detour of the driver's own. The record places the driven segment up to 2273 m away from the optimal route [F3] and the driver's own account says only that he "went round" [F11]; the rider's complaint states the route was not faster. The only signal of faster traffic is on KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY (band 2, 10–19 km/h, 16:54–17:24) [F12], but that band's window expires exactly when the segment begins, and RD-4(b) bands alone do not exempt a segment (G3); there is no traffic incident anywhere on the optimal route [F15], so RD-4(a) is not met. The vehicle's large distance from that expressway is therefore not explained by any rider-authorised route. Finding: counts, ground = driver_errand — nothing in the record ties the 7.53 km loop to a route the rider authorised (the driver states only a verbal "any faster way was fine" [F11], which is a claim, not consent, G11; the chat's own words do not describe the loop).

Amount (RD-2, metered): unexempted extra km = 7.53 km × $1.4099/km = $10.6165 → $10.62. The rater used for the segment is this trip's own distance fare ÷ distance km [F4] ($1.4099/km), consistent with RD-2/G10. Not refunded: the 0.67 km (8.20 − 7.53) of excess distance outside the identified segment (200 m corridor/matching noise) [F1][F4]; the time component of the detour (no published basis in the fare table, G5); the waiting fee $0.11, which is a valid metered waiting unit on a RydeTAXI trip (RD-3(c), RD-2); and all other published items — base, time fare, platform $1.47 [F7]. No unpublished/misdeclared add-on exists, so FARE-1/FARE-2 give nothing.

Flag: RD-6 requires either a refund > 0 (yes) AND route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1 — the driver's profile shows 2 upheld disputes but route disputes = 0 [F18], so "repeated route offence" is not made out; no flag_account.

segment_findings.reason: Rider's only pre-segment message [F9] is a general route authorisation ("哪条快走哪条"), which under RD-5 covers only the route chosen to reach the destination, not the driver's own loop; the driver's post-trip claim that the rider verbally agreed to "any faster way" [F11] is a claim, not consent (G11). The record places the segment up to 2273 m off the optimal route [F3] and nothing ties it to a route the rider authorised; no traffic incident on the optimal route [F15], and the band-2 record on KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY [F12] ends exactly when the segment starts and cannot exempt it (RD-4(b), G3). Unexempted under RD-1 → RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's post-trip statement that the rider verbally agreed to a faster way is a claim about consent, not the rider's own pre-detour message; RD-5/G11 require the rider's own message sent before the detour, and [F9] contains no agreement to this loop.

KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY band 2 (10–19 km/h) covers 16:54–17:24 and is not an LTA incident on the optimal route; a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment (RD-4(b)/G3), and there is no traffic incident at all near the route [F15].
